items.summary_en:
When managers ask me how to train their nontechnical team on AI, my advice is always the same: run an install party

Everyone brings a laptop & you install the agents right there on their machines & get them to complete a meaningful task on the spot. Skip the abstract talk. Once it's installed, people start talking to the agent and learning from each other

The setup is 80% the barrier
items.summary_zh:

门槛的 80% 就是安装；一旦跑起来，人自然会开始用、互相学。

items.summary_en:
Sandboxes are hard.

With all the “AI escaping  sandbox” it’s easy to think “wow AI so scary,” but most AI companies, and recent “sandbox providers” are making very basic mistakes.

At Replit we’ve been running sandboxes since 2016 and targeted by every hacker and state actor under the sun. So we learned a thing or two. 

Main advice: Assume zero-days exist — because they do — and think in layers of protection in a zero-trust framework.

More here: https://t.co/3XGY0a1p3P

items.summary_en:
verbalizing one of those aha moments i had that seems retroactively pretty obvious:

if you prioritize pretrain data quality enough that commoncrawl isn't good enough for you, you have to build a Whole Web scraper anyway, and if you wanna keep it current, you have to have indexing, and pretty soon you find yourself having built a total private low-frequency clone of Google as a SIDE PROJECT of pretraining, that you can then also reuse for the agent side inference.

we do know that the labs do use third party search providers, but clearly this is one of those things where developing more and more of your own 1P equivalents is both a competitive advantage and an adversarial target for AEO Batesian Mimicry* that you will not want to share.

* https://t.co/Wa5fMP8bvO
items.summary_zh:
当你嫌 Common Crawl 的预训练数据不够好，就会被迫自己爬全网、建索引、保持更新，最后发现预训练的副产物竟是一套低频私有版 Google，还能拿去喂 agent 推理。

实验室当然会用第三方搜索，但真正的护城河是自建一方搜索能力；它既是竞争优势，也是会被 AEO 伪装攻击盯上的核心资产。

items.author: Aaron Levie
items.bio: ceo @box - your business lives in content. unleash it with AI
items.summary_en:
The takeaway from this incident should not be that AI is scary. It should be that getting security right is incredibly important in the era of agents. 

Given the right tools and task, agents will do whatever it takes to get the job done, assuming enough compute. Thus, a misconfigured system - or something you thought was locked down but wasn’t - will become a risk vector. 

The core implications are less about the trust and safety of AI itself, but instead the work it’s going to take from enterprises to make sure they harden their environments. Lots of real work ahead for most organizations on this front.
items.summary_zh: 这次事件的重点不是“AI 很可怕”，而是智能体时代安全配置不能有半点侥幸。只要工具和任务给到位，智能体会不惜一切完成目标，企业那些以为锁住但其实没锁住的系统，都会变成风险入口。

items.author: Aaron Levie
items.bio: ceo @box - your business lives in content. unleash it with AI
items.summary_en:
The cost of AI - normalized for the type of task - coming down is one of the most important factors in being able to drive further AI diffusion in the economy.

The general trend we should expect is that frontier AI models will continue to become more capable, and will look very expensive because the tasks that they can take on are more advanced. 

Then, shortly after, AI models will get more efficient or competition will drive more aggressive pricing dynamics, thus reducing the cost per task for anything other than the peak of the frontier.

This cycle will continue over and over again, which ultimately leads to tasks becoming cheaper on a like for like basis. And by doing so you will get even more AI adoption because now AI is more affordable for a wider variety of use-cases.
items.summary_zh:
AI 的真实成本要按任务类型归一化看：前沿模型会因为能干更难的活显得很贵，但很快效率提升和竞争定价会把同类任务成本打下来。

这个循环会反复发生，直到越来越多任务被压成便宜货，AI 才会真正渗进更广泛的经济场景。

These are not the tokens you're gonna find online. Like, you can't crawl Reddit and find out about what happened on a construction site. The Samsara system, in a given day, we're driving 99% of The US roads, usually multiple times a day. I was just in the field last week with a large energy utility, and they shared with me a really interesting stat. They said over the last hundred twenty five years, we built a certain amount of grid capacity.

Speaker 1 | 00:21 - 00:31

Speaker 2 | 00:31 - 00:49
Hi. I'm Matt Turk. Welcome to the MAD podcast. My guest today is Sandeep Biswas, cofounder and CEO of Sensera, the $20,000,000,000 company running what might be the largest AI deployment in the physical world. We talked about physical AI, agents for truckers and frontline workers, humanoids, autonomous trucks, and why the AI boom is really an infrastructure construction project.
